sourcePolicy: multi-source corroboration required; later political arrangements are not back-projected

anchors.name: Alanya/Alaiye
anchors.assessment: Karaman-linked local polity; Memluk suzerainty/coinage context
anchors.notes: TDV identifies Karaman-linked beys after 1293; 1321/1326/1329 coin evidence associates Alaiye with Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad. Do not model as direct Mamluk provincial territory.

anchors.name: Anamur/Mamure
anchors.notes: Early Seljuk conquest was followed by Karamanid control in the Kameruddin-ili tradition. The Mamure complex has Karamanid phases; an official local source associates Ak Camii with 1326 but explicitly notes the surviving inscription is not original, so this is corroboration rather than a precise dating proof.

anchors.name: Mut
anchors.notes: Karamanid origins and Kameruddin-ili sources consistently place Mut in the core southern Karaman zone. Sertavul-Mut corridor links Central Anatolia to the Mediterranean.

anchors.name: Gulnar
anchors.notes: Multiple historical syntheses place Gulnar within the Kameruddin-ili/Karaman sphere; avoid treating later İçel administrative limits as 1326 geometry.

anchors.name: Silifke
anchors.assessment: uncertain in 1326; do not promote to canonical Karaman polygon
anchors.notes: TDV Silifke explicitly argues the city probably entered Karamanid control later, before 1359, despite later narrative traditions assigning it earlier. This is a critical chronology guard.

anchors.name: Korykos/Gorgos (Kizkalesi)
anchors.notes: Archaeological study records Lusignan capture in 1361 and subsequent struggle with Karamanids. Therefore later Karamanid control must not be back-projected to 1326.

anchors.name: Manavgat
anchors.assessment: autonomous local polity with Karamanid/Mamluk patronage context; exact 1326 control unresolved
anchors.notes: A numismatic/historical study argues Manavgat rulers accepted Karamanid rule under Mamluk patronage after weakening Mongol control around 1320; evidence is indirect and later narratives should not be converted into a hard 1326 polygon.

anchors.name: Gazipasa/Selinti
anchors.notes: Modern institutional and geographic studies show succession of Seljuk, Teke and Karamanid control, but do not establish a precise 7 April 1326 boundary. Keep as a control-confidence band.

negativeControls.name: Korykos
negativeControls.reason: Lusignan capture dated 1361; later Karamanid conflict cannot establish Karamanid control in 1326.

negativeControls.name: Silifke
negativeControls.reason: TDV chronology states Karamanid control was probably later than commonly repeated early narratives, before 1359.

modelingRules: Do not derive a continuous coastal Karamanid polygon from later 14th-century control.
Separate local autonomy, suzerainty, tribute and direct territorial control.
Use fort/port/road anchors independently from political ownership.
Treat the Sertavul-Mut-Goksu corridor as a major geographic/logistical connector.
Keep source disagreement in provenance rather than silently resolving it.
